Hi Chloe —

We started noticing intermittent reconnects from our on-prem agents this morning around 02:30 UTC. Most sessions recover within 10–30s, but a small fraction (≈1%) fail to re-establish and require manual restart. Symptoms point at TCP resets and a burst of ICMP unreachable messages from the edge peer.

Attached is a short tcpdump from one of the agents (stratus-ping-traces-20260907.pcap). We're running Redwood Private (vpc) with a single egress NAT gateway in our colo; the NAT mapping looks stable most of the time.

Can you confirm whether any egress rewrite rules or rate-limiting were changed on Redwood's side? We haven't touched our side. This is impacting heartbeat telemetry and a couple of production jobs.

Appreciate any quick guidance.

Folks —

I pulled NAT counters and kernel logs from the egress NAT hosts serving StratusHealth for the window Alex provided. Findings so far:

- NAT port churn is within expected bounds but we see periodic spikes of 4–5k ephemeral port translations torn down within 1s windows (likely due to RSTs).
- There's a short burst of ICMP frag-needed messages right before some of the RSTs. Packet sizes in the pcap show MSS ~1460 but we have an MTU override on the colo link at 1452; fragmentation behaviour looks inconsistent between hosts.
- No kernel OOM or conntrack table exhaustion. Conntrack high-water is ~70% of configured limit.

Action items I propose:
1) Temporarily enable explicit MSS clamp on the egress path for StratusHealth's prefix to 1400 and monitor for 12 hours.
2) Ask Equinix peer to confirm whether any ACLs or ICMP rate-limits are configured on the crossconnect.
3) Request the Stratus agent team to provide a short-ish continuous tcpdump (30m) during their next heartbeat window to validate path MTU.

I'm attaching a config diff showing the proposed MSS clamp and the brief pcap snippet we already have.

-Karthik

Hi all —

We validated the crossconnect ACLs and BGP policies for the pair of ports used by StratusHealth. No ACL denies observed. There is an ICMP policing profile on the aggregation switch that will drop ICMP at a burst threshold (default is 50pps burst, sustained 10pps) which could explain intermittent frag-needed suppression during floods.

We do see flapping microbursts from the customer's side that coincide with the time window. If you enable MSS clamping at 1400 as suggested, that should reduce the need for frag-needed ICMP on the path and avoid relying on Equinix-sent ICMP.

If you'd like, we can temporarily raise the ICMP policing thresholds for the affected ports while you monitor. Let us know the port IDs and desired window.

Regards,
Equinix Peering Support

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent disconnects from on-prem agents — remediation plan & next steps

Alex / team —

Summary and planned remediation:

- Root cause (probable): Path MTU mismatch combined with ICMP policing at the colo edge. Large packets triggered frag-needed; those ICMPs were dropped/intermittently suppressed at the aggregation layer, leading to later TCP retransmits and transient RSTs which tore down NAT mappings.

- Immediate actions taken:
  * Enabled MSS clamp of 1400 on Redwood egress for StratusHealth prefix (applied 2026-09-09T15:05:00-07:00).
  * Requested Equinix to raise ICMP policing on the affected ports for a 24h observation window (Equinix confirmed they applied a temporary increase).
  * Collected extended tcpdump (30m) and compared pre/post — attached as config_diff-egress-20260908.txt summarizing the before/after counters.

- Observed result: After the MSS clamp, we saw a ~90% reduction in frag-needed occurrences and no new persistent agent failures in the 24h observation window. A small number of transient reconnects (0.1%) remained during high traffic bursts; these correlate with the customer's edge flattening (seen in their ingress counters).

Next steps / recommendations:
1) Stratus ops: schedule a maintenance window to validate MTU settings end-to-end (switches/firewalls) and remove any local overrides that may prevent PMTU discovery.
2) Redwood: we'll keep MSS clamp in place as a temporary mitigation and instrument per-port alerting to detect frag-needed suppression.
3) Equinix: continue elevated ICMP thresholds for 48h and then revert while we monitor; we may request a permanent adjustment if transient suppression continues.

I'll close the escalated incident after 72h with no recurrence. Thanks to everyone for the quick collaboration. Please reply if you'd like this rolled into a formal postmortem.

Best,
